Dickson County, TN Tax Sales: A Simple Guide for Buyers

Buying property at a tax sale in Dickson County, Tennessee, can be a smart way to invest. But it’s not like buying a house the regular way. These auctions follow their own rules, and if you’re new to the process, it helps to know what to expect. This guide walks you through how it works—from auction day to getting the deed.

Quick Look: Dickson County Tax Sale Details

How the Tax Sale Process Works

  1. Properties Listed in Newspaper
    About 2–3 weeks before the sale, properties are published in the Dickson Herald.
  2. Registration On-Site
    Show up on the auction day at the Justice Center.
    Registration starts at 10:00 AM; bring a photo ID.
  3. Auction Day
    The sale begins at 11:00 AM.
    Live bidding happens in the courtroom. Highest bid wins.
    Starting bid equals total owed in taxes, interest, and court fees.
  4. Immediate Payment
    Winning bidders must pay right away using cash, money order, or certified check.
  5. Court Confirms the Sale
    The Chancery Court must approve the sale for it to go through.
  6. Redemption Period
    Property owners have 1 year to buy the property back by paying everything owed.
  7. Receiving the Deed
    If not redeemed, the buyer receives the deed and becomes the legal owner.

Where to Get Tax Sale Info

  • Visit the for auction details and court approval process.
  • Use the Tennessee Trustee Portal to view property info and delinquencies.
  • Visit the Dickson County Government Site for general updates.

What to Do Before You Bid

  • Do Your Research
    Use parcel maps and tax records to check property conditions and ownership history.
  • Inspect From Outside
    You can drive by properties, but you can’t enter them.
  • Check for Liens
    Some properties might still have debts like mortgages or city fines attached.
  • Understand the Costs
    Be prepared for additional court costs, legal fees, and title clearing expenses.

After You Win a Property

  • You must pay immediately at the sale.
  • Wait for 12 months before taking full ownership.
  • If the property is not redeemed, you may need a quiet title action for insurance.
  • If someone is still living in the property, you must follow legal eviction procedures.

Why Invest in Dickson County?

A Growing Suburban Area Near Nashville

Dickson County is about 40 minutes west of Nashville. As the city grows, more people are moving here for affordable homes and more space.

Affordable Property and Steady Growth

  • Average home value is around $346,000
  • Strong rental demand for single-family homes
  • More affordable than nearby counties like Williamson or Davidson

Lots of Open Land

Dickson County still has many open parcels, making it attractive for homesteads or long-term development.

Pro Tips for New Buyers

  • Bring certified payment—no personal checks allowed.
  • Always get legal advice, especially for title issues.
  • Look into zoning and building rules.
  • Budget for hidden costs like repairs or back utility bills.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I get the property right after winning?
No. You must wait one year in case the owner redeems the property.

Can anyone bid?
Yes, anyone can bid as long as they register on-site and show valid ID.

Are tax sales online in Dickson County?
No. All auctions are in person only.

Will I be responsible for other debts on the property?
Yes. Some debts may not be cleared by the tax sale. Research is key.

What if someone is living in the property I won?
You may need to go through a legal eviction process.
